summary: Hubert Durt was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte (~1955–1962). He served at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, directed the Hōbōgirin Institute (~1980–2005), and was a professor at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~2001–2018).

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied under doctoral supervisor Wendy Doniger (~1993–1998), Bruce Lincoln, and Tony K. Stewart. He served as Associate Professor of Comparative Studies at Ohio State University (~2004–2007).
Hugh Gray was an Indology scholar who studied at Battersea Grammar School and held an attested post at the University of Cambridge in 1983.
Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who studied at Stanford University. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna, the University of Klagenfurt, and the University of Turin.
Hugh Richardson was a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied at Keble College (~1924–1928) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1930–1950).

Hugo David is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed his PhD at École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2012. He held a fellowship at the University of Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member at École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2015.
Hui-tzu Lu is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who studied under Jing-shen Tao and traditional teachers Zhiru Shi and Zhihui Shi.
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang (attested 2011).

Huimin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He held professorships at Taipei National University of the Arts and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and was President of Dharma Drum Buddhist College (~2007–2014).
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kuo-wei Liu, and also studied under Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.

Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and held an attested lecturer position at Dongguk University in 1996.

Humberto Maturana was a philosopher and scientist who studied at Liceo Manuel de Salas, University College London (~1953–1954), and Harvard University (~1954–1958). He held a post at the University of Chile (~1960–2000).
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon.

Huston Smith was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Central Methodist University and the University of Chicago. He held professorships at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1958–1973), UC Berkeley (~1984), and Syracuse University (attested 2000).
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, where she studied under Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2015).

Hyejeong Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who earned a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She also served as a Visiting Researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies practitioner who studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), Harvard University (~1989–1992), and the University of Freiburg (~1987–1988), and trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn (~1990–2004).

Hyoung Seok Ham is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Virginia (2010) and earned a PhD at the University of Michigan under doctoral supervisor Madhav M. Deshpande (attested 2016).

Hürelbaatar Ujeed is a scholar of religious, Buddhist, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who earned a PhD in Social Anthropology at the University of Cambridge. He held positions at Cambridge (attested 2010) and Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.
